subject: Foray #1 — grilling & world barbecue
purpose: Prioritised ASR work order, re-sorted against the 40-beat spine (docs/curation/grilling-history-spine.md) on 2026-08-17. Priority 1 is the material that would move a CHAIN beat off empty, Act IV first. That ordering is the whole point: 19 of the 24 empty beats are in chains and 5 are in the fan, and a hole in a chain reads to a listener as a missing link while a hole in a fan reads as a change of subject. So a fan hole is cheap and a chain hole is not, and CPU should be spent accordingly. Rows that buy an already-strong beat, that buy no beat at all, or that are unusable under the English-only ruling carry `priority: null` and a `blocked_by` reason. They are kept, never pruned.

revision_2026_08_18.what_changed: Two things, and the first is the one a reader should hold on to. (1) EVERY ROW THAT CARRIED A PRIORITY HAS NOW BEEN TRANSCRIBED. All nine queued episodes were spent across the 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18 passes, so this work order contains no remaining ASR work at all and `queued_episodes` is 0. (2) The search therefore moved off this manifest and onto data/discover.json's 1,534 items, and the result is recorded in `catalogue_search_2026_08_18` below.
revision_2026_08_18.the_headline: Act IV cannot be closed from the catalogue. None of its seven empty chain beats — 16, 17, 20, 25, 26, 28, 29 — has any candidate in data/discover.json, because the catalogue holds no American barbecue history of any kind. That is a buy-or-make finding, not a keep-transcribing one.
revision_2026_08_18.what_the_nine_bought: Nine episodes and about 5.4 hours of audio moved five beats, all of them from one episode (The Grill Coach). The other eight moved none. Every judgement this manifest recorded in advance held, which is why the recommendation below is about stops rather than about sort order.
revision_2026_08_18.the_rule_now_applied: A row this manifest judges would not move a beat carries `stop: true` and `blocked_by: "stop"`, not a low priority. That is grilling-history-coverage.md §9's own recommendation, arrived at after a seven-episode pass that moved nothing: 'a row whose `beat_verdict` is `strong` or whose `why_this_priority` says depth rather than rescue should be treated as a stop, not a low priority — the manifest already contains the judgement, and priority ordering is the wrong instrument for expressing "do not buy this."'

stop_convention.stop: true: Do not buy this row. It is kept, never pruned, and the reason is stated in `stop_reason`. A stop is not a rejection of the episode as listening — see `label_never_exclude`.
stop_convention.blocked_by: \"spent\": Already transcribed. `outcome` records what it moved, which for eight of the nine is nothing.
stop_convention.blocked_by: \"stop\": Never transcribed and should not be. The row failed a specific beat's own reject line, and `stop_reason` names the beat and the line.
stop_convention.priority: null: Carries no claim on CPU. Ten rows carry it for the English-only ruling, six because no beat in the spine covers them, one as superseded by a re-release, and after this revision nine more as spent.
stop_convention.label_never_exclude: Nothing here is removed from data/discover.json or from any playlist. A stop says an episode does not advance a beat of THIS Foray; several of the stops below are good recommendations for other subjects and are wanted as such.

method.ad_free_ratio: delivered bytes / feed-declared enclosure length, via a 2-byte ranged GET reading the true total from Content-Range (tools/transcribe/ad-inflation.mjs). HEAD lies on ad-inserting hosts and was not used. Threshold < 1.01.
method.true_duration: itunes:duration from the feed, cross-checked against declared_bytes*8/duration landing on a standard bitrate. Rows where the feed declares length=0 or length=1 cannot use the byte method and are labelled bitrate-implied.
method.duration_gaps: None. Every row below carries an itunes:duration read from its feed; there is no row whose true duration could not be obtained.

Note that data/transcript-availability.json records 1,858 episodes on that feed of which 12 carry a <podcast:transcript> tag, and only one is on plot: the Moss BBQ School episode already segmented.

Ships a timed transcript and needs no ASR, and is EXCLUDED on the register rather than on availability: two hosts working from an article, no guest, no sourced expertise, and it contains the line that barbecue 'kind of transcends race and class' twenty seconds after its Jim Crow passage — which is the harmony version beat 23 exists to reject. Admitting a source the narrative refutes is the failure #226 was opened to fix. This returns beats 7, 19, 24 and 30 to empty and to narration.

episodes.unlocks: American arc — HAND-OFF, not this workstream's.

Described as covering indigenous roots, the shift to what we now call barbecue, the African American contribution, and the present — beats 18, 20, 21, 22 and 38. Measured ad-free at ratio 1.0, so it needs ASR and nothing else: no probes, no locate step. Adrian Miller is named in the spine itself as the archetype of the register wanted.

We need TIMINGS ONLY — force-align the existing clean prose rather than transcribe from scratch. If the pipeline can emit word timings against supplied text, this row costs a fraction of full ASR and the same trick unlocks all 8 transcript-bearing Moreish episodes.
episodes.unlocks: The jerk slot, which today holds only a framing passage (P5).
episodes.why_this_priority: Turns a framing-only slot into a real one, and is the cheapest row here if timings-only alignment is available.
episodes.buys: Beat 15 is already carried by two cuts from this episode, so this is not depth for its own sake: the episode's publisher transcript is UNTIMED, which is precisely why beat 2's preservation passage cannot be cut separately from beat 15's carrier today. A timed transcript would let beat 2 have its own cut instead of double-booking one passage across two beats — moving a chain beat in Act I from thin toward carried.
episodes.outcome: MOVED NOTHING, and it is the one row in the batch with a specific falsifiable hypothesis, which this pass falsified. It was bought because 'a timed transcript would let beat 2 have its own cut instead of double-booking one passage across two beats'. The timings arrived and timings were never the blocker: every usable preservation sentence sits inside the two cuts that already exist, and the mechanism beat 2 is actually about is absent from the episode at every timestamp.
episodes.stop_reason: Spent. Already in the pool as `moreish-jerk-jamaica`, already cut twice, and already beat 15's carrier at the two-segment maximum. The stated purchase for beat 2 does not complete.
